question: If the height of a tower is √3 times its shadow, then the angle of the elevation of the top of the tower is equal to:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The relationship between **Height** (H) and **Shadow** (S) is given as H = √3 × S.

In a right-angled triangle, **tan θ** = Height ÷ Shadow.

⇒ tan θ = (√3 × S) ÷ S = √3.

Since tan 60° = √3, the **Angle of Elevation** is 60°.

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Height of the tower (h) = √3 × length of shadow (s).

**Formula Used:** tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/19ae3629dc4c1f81d2185f6d20d8e3c5cfbfe1075f708fd694de45a3573205a1.png] 

Let the length of the **Shadow** (BC) be x units.

⇒ **Height** of the tower (AB) = √3x units.

In right ΔABC, let the **Angle of Elevation** ∠ACB = θ.

⇒ tan θ = AB ÷ BC

⇒ tan θ = √3x ÷ x

⇒ tan θ = √3

⇒ tan θ = tan 60°

⇒ θ = 60°

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios for Standard Angles

Common values: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3, and tan 90° is undefined.

Angle of Elevation and Depression

The **Angle of Elevation** is the angle between the horizontal line and the line of sight when looking up at an object.

Height and Shadow Property

When the angle of elevation is 45°, the height of the object is exactly equal to the length of its shadow.</p
